correctness.rationale: A full 76-row integer boundary computation reconstructs all 45 signed third boundaries and 20 oriented octahedral cycles. Boundary ranks are independently bounded modulo 101; a 39-by-39 determinant -1 unit minor makes 35 boundary generators plus four octahedral cycles a primitive full second-cycle lattice. Exact integer reconstruction of all third-boundary columns proves rank 35 and the free quotient Z^4. All 20 sphere vectors have primitive exact integral coordinates. Graph automorphisms enumerated exhaustively (48) give orbit sizes 8 and 12 and Smith diagonals (1,1,1,1) and (1,1,1). A flag-link argument proves minimal support six, checked exhaustively for 924 six-subsets. Finite computation is fully reproducible, not an infinite-family proof.

value.rationale: The Franklin graph is a canonical symmetric 12-vertex cubic graph, and octahedral spheres are the geometrically shortest possible flag-complex second-homology carriers. Its two natural octahedral automorphism orbits have sharply different lattice-generating strengths: the smaller orbit generates the complete integral H2, while the larger has a primitive rank-three image missing one entire rational direction. This is a structural symmetry and integral representability distinction not supplied by the Betti number, ordinary homotopy rank, or routine exact enumeration alone.
